niche_preference_profile: This user consistently prefers clean, spacious interfaces with strong visual hierarchy, rounded components, and modular content grouping. They favor centered or tightly grouped focal content, simplified compositions with limited decorative clutter, and clearer scannability through bullets, sectioning, and concise blocks. They often respond well to soft or premium visual treatments such as gradients, blurred backgrounds, isolated modals, and high-contrast card layouts, while rejecting cramped, dense, monolithic, or overly embellished screens. They also show repeated preference for clearer iconography, visible primary content, and balanced button emphasis rather than harsh or overly heavy controls.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers generous spacing, breathing room, open margins, and fewer visible elements at once; rejects cramped, compressed, or tightly packed layouts.

Prefers interfaces where the main message or primary information is prominent through centered focus, larger headlines, clear sectioning, and better grouping; rejects weaker emphasis and less differentiated structure.
Prefers cleaner screens with fewer decorative or distracting elements, less chrome, and more focused composition; rejects embellished, noisy, or visually busy layouts.
Prefers softer, more rounded corners on cards and controls, including rounded buttons and pill-like or softened shapes; rejects sharper rectangular treatments.
Prefers content broken into modular cards, grouped sections, bullets, and concise summary blocks that are easy to scan; rejects monolithic panels, dense grids, and long uninterrupted text.
Prefers visually refined surfaces such as gradients, blurred or subdued backgrounds, and strong card-to-background contrast that isolates content; rejects flat, muddy, or low-separation backgrounds.

Prefers clearly visible key content and controls, including legible icons, visible artwork, distinct headers, and readable primary data displays; rejects low-contrast, missing, or less immediately readable primary elements.
